Product foundation / Signal visualization

Instrument software platform

An extensible desktop application foundation for instrument control, measurement workflows and engineering interfaces.

C++ / QtIQ visualizationOpenGL

A shared foundation for instrument applications

The platform brings device control, measurement workflows and reusable desktop interfaces together. Signal visualization components provide a common way to inspect IQ data across different instrument modes.

The examples below show an IQ visualization development interface using a generated 16QAM signal. They illustrate component behavior rather than measured hardware performance.

Constellation density view

A density-colored constellation makes sample concentrations and the spread around symbol positions visible. The interface exposes block size, signal selection and noise controls, alongside pause and clear-density actions.

Eye diagram and interactive markers

The eye view overlays signal trajectories across a two-unit-interval display. M1 and M2 controls and marker readouts support inspection of positions within the plot, while density coloring highlights frequently occurring trajectories.

Reusable visualization components

Constellation, eye and I/Q time tabs share the signal controls. This component approach gives instrument applications a consistent inspection workflow while allowing each view to present the data in its own coordinates.

  • Shared input context. Keep signal and block settings close to the active visualization.
  • Rendering and interaction. Combine density displays with pause, reset and marker controls.
  • Application integration. Organize visualization components alongside device control and measurement modes in the broader platform.
